To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) FH is not a monolithic disorder but a heterogeneous condition with a wide range of phenotypic expressions; (2) the diagnosis of FH is not based solely on LDL cholesterol levels; and (3) FH can be caused by a variety of genetic defects in the LDLR, apoB, or PCSK9 genes and, therefore, can present with different clinical manifestations and responses to treatment.

1) the LDLR and apoB mutations in FH patients are not the only cause of FH; 2) mutations in the PCSK9 gene are responsible for 10% of the cases; and 3) the prevalence of the disease is much higher than previously estimated.

the identification of the molecular basis of FH, the characterization of the phenotypic expression of the disease, the development of a strategy for the prevention and management of the disease, and the identification of the mechanisms of the disease in order to develop a cure.
the development of a new approach to the study of the effect of the disease on the disease.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
a genetic cause for FH should be suspected if the LDL cholesterol level is above the 99th percentile in a young adult with no other risk factors and if there is a positive family history.
a genetic cause for the elevated LDL cholesterol levels is not excluded.

a diagnosis of FH should not be made on the basis of a single lipid measurement, and the diagnosis should be based on a detailed history of the patient and family and on the clinical presentation, which should include xanthomas and tendon xanthomas.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed a novel approach to identify FH patients with a high probability of having a mutation in the LDLR or apoB gene.
the genetic basis of the most common forms of hyperlipidemia is still not fully elucidated, and the diagnosis of FH in the absence of other risk factors is not straightforward.

there is a strong association between the presence of the apoE2 allele and a lower risk of CHD in patients with hypercholesterolaemia and that this association was independent of the presence of the E2/E2 genotype and the apoE4 allele.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the genetic diagnosis of FH should be based not only on the presence of a mutation in LDLR or APOB but also on the severity of the phenotype, which can be determined by the LDL cholesterol level and the presence of other clinical features.
the clinical phenotype of FH is highly variable and can be influenced by many factors other than the underlying LDLR genotype.
there are 2 types of FH, and the distinction between them is not always obvious.
